findings.message: Task 3.1's own description and Architectural Decision commit to removing `/conversation/opening` and `/conversation/judge` from `backend/app/main.py` ("This task removes their route handlers... and their entries from docs/conversation-backend-api.md"), but both routes are still live in `main.py` (lines 215-235, 237-239) and still documented (docs/conversation-backend-api.md's own 'Retiring' section admits this). The reason is real and well-documented: `backend/tests/test_health.py` and `backend/tests/test_pipeline.py` exercise these routes directly to prove task 1.1's CORS/concurrency/501 contract and task 1.2's judge behavior, and rewriting those tests to exercise the same properties through the session endpoints instead is substantial, cross-cutting work (verified: test_health.py's five judge/opening-route tests are the *only* vehicle it has for proving CORS-allow, CORS-reject, and the two-call concurrency/health-stays-responsive behavior). `ConversationPracticePort`'s own doc comment compounds this by asserting a falsehood: "their backend routes are retired in the same phase (task 3.1)" (ConversationPracticePort.ts line ~15) — the frontend side is retired, the backend side is not. Net effect: the plan's stated trust-boundary mitigation (retiring dead surface reachable by any local origin, per the plan README's Trust Boundary Inventory) was not actually delivered, and no task in phase 3 owns the fix — task 3.1 explicitly scoped it out, task 3.3 explicitly declined to touch it (documented in its own Manual Verification section) as being outside its covers.
findings.why_not_fixed: Fixing this safely means rewriting backend/tests/test_health.py's CORS/concurrency/501 proofs and backend/tests/test_pipeline.py's opening/judge happy-path proofs to exercise the same properties through the session endpoints instead — those files prove tasks 1.1/1.2's acceptance criteria, which are outside this phase's diff and already-settled. I cannot bound the blast radius of that rewrite from here (whether the session endpoints can even express a 'models not loaded yet' 501 state the same way, whether CORS needs its own now-route-agnostic test) without redoing work that belongs to a dedicated task, which is exactly what task 3.1's own docs conclude is needed.

options.option: Accept as a documented, deliberate known gap for now (current state)
options.consequence: The dead routes stay reachable by any local origin per the plan's own Trust Boundary Inventory (SA-1/QA-31) — low practical risk on a local-only single-user tool, but the plan's stated mitigation is not actually in place.

options.option: Add a new task (or extend an existing one's covers) to migrate test_health.py/test_pipeline.py's CORS/concurrency/501 proofs onto the session endpoints and then delete the two routes
options.consequence: Closes the gap properly but is real new scope this phase did not budget for.

findings.recommendation: Add a new task (or extend an existing one's covers) to migrate test_health.py/test_pipeline.py's CORS/concurrency/501 proofs onto the session endpoints and then delete the two routes

findings.message: Every unit-level acceptance criterion for tasks 3.2 and 3.3 (AC1-AC7 across both tasks) is marked [NO RED] in the criteria ledger — no red proof was ever recorded for any of them, unlike task 3.1 which has a full red proof for all six of its ACs. I spot-checked one (ConversationUnlockService's boundary logic) by mutating `checkConversationUnlock`'s unlocked condition to always-true and confirmed 3 of 5 tests in ConversationUnlockService.test.ts fail with the expected assertions, then reverted — so the tests that exist are real, not tautological. But this was never done for the other ~12 NO RED criteria (Dashboard gate behavior, ConversationPracticePage's tally/exhaustion/mid-session-failure/blob-revocation logic), so those tests have never been observed catching the regression they claim to guard against.
findings.why_not_fixed: Producing a genuine red proof for each of the remaining ~12 criteria means mutating the corresponding implementation logic (tally accumulation, blob-URL revocation timing, the unavailable-state transition, the Dashboard's onClick gating) one at a time and re-running the suite for each, which is real verification work I did not have budget to do exhaustively in this round; my one spot-check confirms the general pattern (tests assert real behavior, not tautologies) but does not stand in for the missing records for the other criteria.
findings.recommendation: Backfill red proofs for tasks 3.2/3.3's criteria the same way task 3.1 already did (mutate, observe red, restore, record which assertion fired).
